name: MondayBench judge contract v1
purpose: Answer 'did these two evaluations use the same scoring semantics APPLICABLE TO THIS SCENARIO?' - not 'did the repository hold identical global schemas at the moment each was written?'

fingerprint.canonical_json: json.dumps(obj, sort_keys=True, separators=(',',':'), ensure_ascii=True) - key order, whitespace and unicode escaping are all normalised, so serialisation cannot move the hash
fingerprint.legacy_field: Evaluation.judge.prompt_fingerprint is KEPT and never rewritten, so every v1.0 evaluation stays byte-identical and independently readable.

shape.contract_schema_version: str - bumped when this object's shape changes
shape.scenario_prompt_sha256: str - what the candidate was actually asked
shape.ground_truth_sha256: str - over the canonicalised answer key, or the prose text
shape.ground_truth_sliced_per_criterion: bool - whether a ground_truth_map is in force

judge_instructions.noise: same shape, or null when the rubric has no noise dimension

shape.criteria: array IN RUBRIC DECLARATION ORDER. Each entry: id, dimension, points{pass,partial,fail}, the three definitions, and the sorted ground_truth_paths that criterion's judge call may see.
shape.noise: null, or {max_points, starting_points, deduction_per_false_action, minimum_points, false_actions:[{id,description}]}
shape.penalties: array of {type, points, definition}, sorted by type, containing ONLY the penalties this scenario's rubric declares

output_contract.penalty_schema: object whose type.enum is the scenario's penalties

ordering_rules.criteria: declaration order preserved. It is the order the recorded judge reads the rubric in, and reordering a rubric is a rubric edit that should move the hash. This is what makes TEST F meaningful.
ordering_rules.penalties: sorted by type - a dict has no meaningful order

deliberately_excluded: PENALTY_TYPE_VALUES - the global union. THE root cause; replaced by the scenario's own penalty list rather than merely dropped.
timestamps, local paths, YAML comments, file mtimes
any criterion, penalty or false action belonging to another scenario
run-level data: responses, scores, model identity
deliberately_included_that_is_not_today: the rubric itself - criteria, definitions, points, dimensions, the penalty cap
evaluator.prompt_file and evaluator.penalty_prompt_file, the scenario-specific judge instructions that v0.2..v0.5 all declare and that the current fingerprint never reads
the ground truth content and the per-criterion ground_truth_map
